title: Scientists develop moth-eye-inspired antireflective surfaces for PV modules
summary: Researchers in Portugal have investigated the mechanical durability of moth-eye-inspired antireflective silicon surfaces for photovoltaic applications. They found that repeated sliding causes nanopillar fracture and material compaction, with higher mechanical loads leading to increased friction and wear. The post Scientists develop moth-eye-inspired antireflective surfaces for PV modules appeared first on pv magazine Global .
